walk_name: Whimsical London: Charm, Chance, and Colour

points.title: Portobello Road Market
points.description: Portobello Road is at the heart of Notting Hill, where William’s everyday life unfolds. The market represents a version of London that feels personal, vibrant, and full of small, meaningful encounters.

audio.title: Ain’t No Sunshine - Bill Withers
audio.note: Start here. Walk with the flow of the market.

points.title: The Blue Door (280 Westbourne Park Road)
points.description: The famous blue door marks William’s flat in Notting Hill. It’s become a symbol of the film’s charm — ordinary life touched by something unexpected.

audio.title: She - Elvis Costello
audio.note: Pause briefly. This is one of London’s most iconic film locations.

points.title: Travel Bookshop Location
points.description: The original travel bookshop from Notting Hill was located here. Though the shop itself no longer exists, the location still draws visitors, representing the film’s idea that life-changing moments can happen in the most ordinary places.

audio.title: How Can You Mend a Broken Heart
audio.note: Keep walking — this is about moments hidden in everyday spaces.

points.title: Alice’s Antiques (Paddington 2)
points.description: The antique shop from Paddington 2 sits along Portobello Road. In the film, it becomes a place of wonder — full of hidden objects and stories, reflecting Paddington’s sense of curiosity and kindness.

audio.title: Paddington 2 Soundtrack
audio.note: Let this feel lighter — this is the most playful part of the walk.

points.title: Westbourne Park Road (Colorful Houses)
points.description: The pastel-coloured houses of Notting Hill feature heavily in Paddington 2, creating a stylised version of London that feels warm, welcoming, and slightly magical.

audio.title: Rain on the Roof - Paddington 2
audio.note: Slow down and look around — this is London at its most joyful.
